newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Bhutto weeps at brother murder probe.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Bhutto weeps at brother murder probe.

text.p: Pakistan's former prime minister Benazir Bhutto wept as she told a judicial tribunal on Saturday she believed the killing of her estranged brother Murtaza was part of a conspiracy to topple her government.
She accused President Farooq Leghari of conducting psychological warfare against her before sacking her three-year-old government on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
"The plan behind it was to overthrow my government," Bhutto said of Murtaza's death in a September 20 police shootout outside his home in Karachi's seaside Clifton area.

Before attending the three-judge inquiry into the killing, she caressed a black goat at her fortress-like Bilawal House residence where the animal was slaughtered as a traditional sacrifice to ward off evil spirits.
Karachi's Supreme Court building was guarded by more than 100 armed police and para-military rangers.
Bhutto's father Zulfikar Ali Bhutto was toppled as prime minister in a 1977 army coup and executed in 1979 after a controversial conviction for conspiring in the murder of a political opponent.
Her youngest brother Shahnawaz died of suspected poisoning in France in 1985.
Her Pakistan People's Party (PPP) was routed in February 3 elections, which gave a landslide victory to new Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League party.
Bhutto accused unspecified "hidden hands and moving shadows" of conspiring to overthrow her when she decided to move a vote of confidence in the previous National Assembly (lower house).
Leghari denies that he conspired to remove Bhutto, who got him elected as president after 1993 general elections won by the PPP.
Bhutto said Leghari's agenda was to "hijack" the PPP and become the president for a second term. "He wanted to be de facto president and de facto prime minister."

Members of Murtaza's breakaway Shaheed Bhutto faction of the PPP accuse Bhutto's husband Asif Ali Zardari of conspiring in their leader's murder. Zardari, in jail since his wife's ouster, denies the charge.
Bhutto said Murtaza was killed to unsettle her ahead of her dismissal and urged the tribunal to identify the killers. "See the real killers," she said.
